question: Who among the following is the author of the book 'The Hungry Tide'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amitav Ghosh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amitav Ghosh** is a renowned Indian author known for his works of historical and cultural fiction.
 
• The book **'The Hungry Tide'** was published in **2004** and is set in the Sundarbans, a unique mangrove ecosystem in India.
 
• 'The Hungry Tide' explores themes like **ecological conservation, cultural displacement, and human relationships**.
 
• Ghosh has received multiple awards, including the **Padma Shri** (2007) and the **Jnanpith Award** (2018), India's highest literary honor.
 
• Other notable works by Amitav Ghosh include **'The Glass Palace,' 'Sea of Poppies,' and 'Gun Island.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sundarbans:**

 
 
• The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest located in the delta region of the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers.
 
• It is home to the famous **Bengal tiger** and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The region faces challenges like **rising sea levels, climate change, and biodiversity loss.**
 
 
 
• **Ecological Literature:**
 
 
• Ecological literature combines storytelling with themes of environmental conservation and sustainability.
 
• Authors like Amitav Ghosh use their writings to raise awareness about **pressing global ecological issues.**
 
 
 
• **Amitav Ghosh's Recognition:**
 
 
• He was awarded the **Jnanpith Award** in 2018 for his outstanding contribution to Indian literature.
 
• He is one of the few Indian authors writing in English to gain international acclaim for his novels.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• 'The Hungry Tide' incorporates historical elements, such as the **Morichjhanpi massacre of 1979.**
 
• The novel provides insight into the struggles of refugees and marginalized communities in the Sundarbans region.
